Yesterday, I redeemed a free drink from Starbucks after I had accumulated 12 stars on my card. There were several other people claiming their free drinks as well because it was the last day before all stars earned in 2015 would expire.

I usually order iced Americano, but since this was a free drink, I thought I would indulge a bit by getting an iced roasted caramel macchiato.

The barista behind the counter said that I could add 15 pesos (30 cents in USD) to make my drink go from grande to a venti, and that I could get an add-on for free, so if I wanted, I could have additional caramel syrup to my drink to increase the flavor. I said no, I didn't even want the free grande size, so could she please downgrade it to tall instead? She looked a bit surprised, but thankfully didn't push it. I also requested non-fat milk to be used in my drink.

As I waited for my order to be processed, I watched the person behind me place her order. Like me, she was claiming her free drink before her stars expired. But unlike me, she was a smallfat who could definitely stand to lose around at least 20 pounds. Unsurprisingly, she got a grande white mocha frappe with additional hazelnut and caramel syrup. So this means she not only upgraded to grande and took her free add-on, but she also bought an extra add-on. I couldn't help but be amazed at how different our definitions of indulgence are. Just seeing her drink before I left made me nauseous. The heavy whipped cream on top of it didn't help.

(Added: It did cross my mind that maybe she was saving all her calories for the day for her beetus drink, but even if that were true, why celebrate when you haven't finished the race yet?)

Your complaint is that it feels like a waste; time that could have been better spent doing something productive, but can't that be said of pretty much any entertainment? Reading a book, watching a movie, playing sports.. I think your problem isn't that they are a waste of time, it's that your entertainment needs have changed, and the games you are used to meeting those needs are no longer doing so.
As I've gotten older, I've definitely changed how I play video games dramatically. I went from having scores and scores of lengthy, often obscure SNES&PlayStation-era RPGs under my belt, with a whole slew of 100% completion saves, to simply not having the patience or room in my life for those sorts of time-commitments anymore. Hell, I don't even understand like, the last 4-5 Final Fantasy games and spin-offs.
But I still play a lot of smaller games, especially short indie games or casual games that let me pick up the controller and set it back down half an hour or so later, and I still really love having friends over for Mario Party style games (or physical board games). Stuff that probably wouldn't have held my attention like a good story or a Civilization run-through would have, back in the day. My point is that your slump is more likely to be related to your life changing in general, and that trying some different styles of games might fix your funk.
